title: Workspace Lattice: Navigation proposals & sprint notes
body:
Purpose and scope:
This note collects our early proposals and sprint-level grooming for a rethought console navigation that centers around 'workspaces' and a lattice of task entrances rather than a strict hierarchical rail. The goal is to reduce cognitive switching for multi-route flows (e.g., model experiments -> rollouts -> metrics) while making it easy to reason about SLO/route ownership and to support future composition (compact views, embeddable routes).

High-level thesis (1 paragraph):
Current sidebar hierarchy is too rigid for users who operate across models, routes, and environments concurrently. Propose a lattice approach: surfaces are organized by task-entry anchors (Build, Observe, Operate, Ship) mapped to contextual workspaces (model-centric, route-centric, org-wide). Each workspace exposes a small set of task entrances (cards) that route to a consistent URL contract. This reduces deep nesting and supports quick switching + persistent session anchors.

Wireframe writeup (sketch-level descriptions):
- Workspace bar (top-left): a compact pill row showing active workspaces with quick-switch hotkeys. Sketch: 40px tall pills, left aligned, overflow into a searchable dropdown. Behavior: keyboard nav cycles, Ctrl+K to open workspace switcher with fuzzy search.
- Lattice sidebar (left): vertical rail that contains grouped task entrances rather than full pages. Grouping example: Model X workspace -> Entrances: Overview, Versions, Serve Config, Load Tests, Traces. Each entrance is a single-click entry point that may open as a panel or full page depending on deep-link flag.
- Session anchor strip (floating): small horizontal strip near page header that persists the last 2–3 clicked entrances for the current workspace (session history). Allows quick back-to-recent without browser backchain.
- Deep link behavior: entrances map to canonical URLs like /workspace/{id}/entrance/{slug}?anchor={sessionId}. Entrance pages must include a small breadcrumb that shows workspace -> entrance and an optional child view (e.g., rollout detail).

Routing / contract details (notes for eng):
- Canonical route components: {workspace_type}/{workspace_id}/entrance_slug[/subpage]?version=X&env=Y
- Entrances are first-class routes with internal subviews; sub-views should avoid creating new top-level history entries unless explicit (configurable).
- Fallback routing: when an entrance is removed (deprecated), requests should redirect to /workspace/{id}/entrance/overview with a 302 client-side toast explaining the redirect and an opt-in link to archive view.

Backlog grooming — candidate tickets and acceptance criteria (sprint-sized):
1) NAV-1010: Workspace pill switcher component (UI): render, keyboard nav, fuzzy search. Acceptance: accessible keyboard nav, search returns <300ms for 1000 workspaces, unit tests.
2) NAV-1013: Lattice sidebar prototype (UX): clickable entrances, collapsible groups. Acceptance: maps to wireframe, supports 3 grouping modes (model, route, org).
3) NAV-1018: Session anchor strip (UX+state): persist last 3 entrances per session, survive refresh. Acceptance: anchored state stored in sessionStorage, visual tests.
4) NAV-1022: URL contracts and redirect middleware (eng infra): canonicalize entrance URLs and implement safe redirect. Acceptance: redirect unit tests, integration with rollout deprecation flow.

Prioritization rationale:
- NAV-1010 first because switching workspaces is the highest-friction for power users (observed in support tickets).
- NAV-1013 next to validate grouping assumptions with a small user panel.
- NAV-1018 low risk but high UX value; implement as session state only initially.
- NAV-1022 needs coordination with infra and releases.

Telemetry & observability to track impact:
- Events: workspace_switch, entrance_click, entrance_open_mode (panel|page), session_anchor_use, redirect_fallback.
- KPIs: median time to first meaningful action after sign-in (goal: -15% after pilot), switches-per-user-per-week (goal: lower is better if combined with successful entrance clicks?), click depth to action (reduce >1-level navigations by 30%).
- Dashboards: per-route conversion funnel (entrance -> primary action), error rates on redirects, performance (p95) of workspace switcher API.

Edge cases & unresolved questions (explicit):
- How to represent multi-ownership items (route shared across two teams)? Proposal: show dual-pill context: small team badges on the entrance card and an ephemeral selector to choose context. Need input from product-ops on billing/ownership model.
- Mobile behavior: lattice rail compresses to a stacked top nav; do we keep workspace pills or replace with a workspace selector modal? UX prefers a modal. Need to prototype.
- Internationalization: pill labels must truncate gracefully; ensure fuzzy search supports diacritics (ask infra for ICU-based comparator).
- Accessibility: ensure keyboard-only discovery of entrances and explicit ARIA roles for session anchors.

Wireframe annotations (developer-friendly):
- Entrance cards: include small secondary action icon (open in new tab / open as panel). Default opening behavior respects user preference (global setting).
- Panel mode: left-snap panel overlays the lattice rail area; panels should be re-entrant (multiple panels stacked with mild z-offset) up to 2 deep.
- Breadcrumbs: condensed format: {workspace-name} › {entrance} › {subview}, clickable.

Grooming notes from workshop (2024-09-25):
- UX research: run 5 moderated sessions with power users (SREs, ML engineers) focusing on multi-model workflows; success criterion: participants accomplish cross-route task without using search > 80% of time.
- Design exploration: two variants for grouping: affinity-based (by task type) and artifact-based (by model/route). We should A/B test with a small cohort.
- Engineering constraints: we must support existing deep links for bookmarks; plan to maintain /model/{id} compatibility via router aliasing for 6 months.

Draft decisions log (temporary):
- Decision 2024-09-30: implement workspace pill switcher and lattice sidebar as opt-in beta behind feature flag 'lattice-nav'.
- Decision pending: session anchors default state (on/off) — requires infra for metrics.

Next steps (short-term):
- Create NAV-1010, NAV-1013, NAV-1018 in Jira, assign owners for sprint-45.
- Design: produce 3 medium-fidelity screens (switcher open, lattice collapsed, lattice expanded + panel) and handoff tokens. Due: 2024-10-09.
- Research: recruit 6 participants for moderated remote testing (complete by 2024-10-18).
- Engineering: spike for URL contract middleware and redirect behavior (2d).

Loose notes / brain dump (keep for iteration):
- Consider heatmap overlay for the lattice showing where users click most — could drive dynamic ordering of entrances.
- Think about a small machine-learning assistant to suggest a workspace based on recent actions and calendar events (long-term).
- Naming: 'Workspace Lattice' might be a working name; alternatives: Task Mesh, Entry Grid. Prefer lattice for now.

Appendix: sample user story (for ticket text)
Title: Quick-switch to model load test
As an ML engineer, I want to switch to the model 'gpt-l6' workspace and start a load test from the Serve > Load Tests entrance so that I can validate new config without going through the route list.
Acceptance criteria: clicking the model pill opens that workspace, the Serve card is visible in the lattice, clicking Load Tests opens the panel with the last test template preselected.

Comments welcome — this is intentionally a sketchy sprint-level doc. Leave notes inline or add to UX-331 for tracked feedback.
